title: The Chinese Towns With No Roads — Only Water | China Travel Expert
description:
Some Chinese towns have no roads at all — you get around by boat.

An hour west of Shanghai lie the water towns of Jiangnan. Zhujiajiao formed as a settlement more than 1,700 years ago, and today canals still thread past a thousand Ming and Qing houses and nine old riverside streets. Thirty-six ancient stone bridges remain — among them Fangsheng Bridge, the largest five-arch stone bridge in East China. It is one of the best-preserved water towns in the region, a slow world of poled boats sitting right beside a modern megacity.

🧭 Expert Tip: Reach Zhujiajiao before 9am — you'll get the canals and bridges almost to yourself before the tour groups arrive.
